description:
Change one custom CSS block: replace its CSS, rename it, switch it on or off, or move it in the order. Fields left out keep their value.

It edits the help center's design DRAFT (its v2 template): the draft the dashboard's Template Editor opens, with a live preview. Nothing reaches visitors until helpcenter_publish_template — after editing, give the customer the Template Editor link from the result to review, and publish only when they ask. v2 help centers only (a classic one answers template_migration_required). Ids come from helpcenter_get_template.

Read the block first (helpcenter_get_template, section 'custom_css' with its id). Switching a block off (enabled:false) shows the design without it and keeps it to switch back on. A theme's blocks are the customer's too, edited in the dashboard (Advanced → Custom CSS): to change how a theme looks, prefer a block of your own (helpcenter_add_template_css), which comes later and wins. This is the guide's `update_css` operation.

Args:
  - id (string): the block.
  - css, label, enabled, index (optional): what to change.
  - etag (string, optional): from your last read or edit; refuses (stale_draft) if the draft changed since.

Returns: what each entry did (new ids), warnings worth relaying, and the draft status with its new etag.

agent_key.description: The api_key helpcenter_create_help_center returned for this help center, exactly as returned. Required on every call: this endpoint has no sign-in, so the key is how each call says which help center it acts on. It is sent to HelpCenter.io as this call's credential and nowhere else, and it is never shown again: keep it for the whole task, and never show it to the user or write it into content.

css.description: The new CSS, replacing the block's.

enabled.description: false switches the block off without deleting it.

etag.description: Optimistic lock: the draft etag from your last read, or the one your last edit returned. When given, the call is refused (stale_draft) if someone changed the draft since — so you never build on a state you have not seen. Omit to apply to the current draft.

id.description: Id of a custom CSS block, as the draft reports it.

index.description: Move the block to this 0-based position among the CSS blocks.

label.description: A name for the block, e.g. 'Cards · hover lift'.

name: helpcenter_update_template_css
title: Change Custom CSS
